headline: Adopted annual general assistance ordinance and approved buying portable traffic signals; advanced fire truck bid and several spending orders.
summary: Councilors confirmed Bruno Inácio as Finance Director and accepted a fourth-quarter unappropriated funds report. Several orders passed first reading, including expenditures for Mill Brook Preserve and the Portland Trails Rock Row Connector Trail. The meeting also included a review of PFAS sampling at three athletic fields.
decisions: Approved purchase of portable traffic signals for Public Services, 6-0-1.
Confirmed the appointment of Bruno Inácio as Finance Director, 6-0-1.
Adopted the annual General Assistance ordinance and the FY 2026-2027 maximums, 6-0-1.
Accepted the unappropriated funds report for the 4th quarter of FY 2026, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of the award of bid for a replacement medium-duty pick-up truck for the Fire Department, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of acceptance of federal asset forfeiture funds, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of an expenditure to Presumpscot Regional Land Trust for Mill Brook Preserve improvements, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of an expenditure for the Portland Trails Rock Row Connector Trail, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of Task Order No. 11 with Credere Associates for supplemental services on Riverwalk North, 6-0-1.
Approved first reading of amendments to several orders on the Landslide Vulnerability Assessment Project and the vendor list, 6-0-1.

WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, OCTOBER 5, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
 
I. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the 
City Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
II. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice-President), Brian McCambridge (Ward 1), Victor 
Chau (Ward 2), Amy Faulkingham (Ward 4)(via Zoom), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, President), Gary Rairdon (At-
Large) 
 
City Councilors Absent: Anna A. Turcotte (Ward 3) 
 
Other City Officials Present: Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi 
(Assistant City Administrator), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Bruno Inácio (Finance Director), Sean Lally 
(Police Chief), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), David Morse (Mayor), Robyn Saunders (Project Manager), Stephen Sloan 
(Fire Chief), Monqiue Cornett (Director of Economic Development), Rebecca Spitella (Director of Planning & 
Code Enforcement), Harrison Deah (Director of General Assistance & Social Services), Doug Eaton (Public 
Services Operations Supervisor) 
 
  
III. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
  
IV. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
No minutes were presented for approval. 
 
  
V. MAYOR'S MESSAGE  
 
 Mayor Morse read his message into the record. A summary is included below: 
• Before the next Council meeting, we will observe Indigenous People's Day on October 12th and 
wanted to acknowledge the significance of this day, and invite the community to learn about 
this history.  
• Mayor Morse invited Through These Doors to accept a Proclamation in honor of Domestic 
Violence Awareness Month during October 2026, and invited representatives of the 
organization to share a few words.  
• Robyn Saunders (Project Manager) provided a review of the PFAS sampling conducted at the 
three (3) athletic fields in Westbrook, and this was done in cooperation with Credere 
Association, University of Connecticut Brownfields Program, & Dave Van Slyke with 
PretiFlaherty. The following Councilors spoke: Councilor Rairdon thanked Robyn Saunders and
the team for the work and care they took on this project. What would a homeowner do if they 
wanted testing on private property? Mayor Morse thanked Robyn and the staff for their time 
of this project.  
 
  
VI. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for City Council messages. Councilors provided the following 
updates: 
• Councilor Rairdon would like to acknowledge Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and Westbrook 
Strong has been donating funds to various organizations that support Domestic Violence victims. If you 
see something that isn't right, say something. 
 
  
VII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
City Clerk Ellis Ledoux provided an update to the City Council on the search for Student Representatives for 
2026-2027. An overview is provided below:  
• At the end of the school year for 2025-2026, the interest in participation was low. The City Clerk's 
Office consulted with City Council & the High School and came to an agreement to readvertize the 
position at the beginning of the 2026-2027 school year.  
• Since the beginning of the school year, we have received a couple of applications, which will be going 
through the review phase with Council Leadership and the City Clerk's Office. 
 
  
VIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: 
 
  
IX. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for consideration.  
 
  
X. ORDERS OF THE DAY (SECOND AND FINAL READING)  
 
 Order 2026-106. Authorizing Purchase of Portable Traffic Signals for Public Services  
 Motion to approve second and final reading of Order 2026-106 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Doug Eaton (Public Services Operation Manager) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-106 adopted. (Vote 6-0-1) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, McCambridge, Chau,Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Turcotte
